key_idea: Write each half-plane excursion as an arc of a scalar profile equation in u = x²/2, fit every arc with a unique quadratic model profile whose (λ, κ) coordinates are transported along a monotone law, then use the sign result (R/G)_r ≤ 0 together with a counting lemma (f' = b·q with q monotone gives at most two zeros) to bound the zeros of the matching function Δ.
reason: The arc-coordinate and quadratic-fit framework is original and does real conceptual work: it reduces counting limit cycles to the zeros of a one-variable matching function whose derivative factors into a monotone quantity. That core is buried under a long chain of technical lemmas, exact algebraic identities, Riccati estimates and a four-way coefficient case split, so the reason the bound is exactly two never feels inevitable; the sharpness half is a standard Melnikov-type computation.
recognized: no (bound on limit cycles of the Liénard system x' = y − F(x), y' = −x with deg F ≤ 5, sharp at two, consistent with the Lins–de Melo–Pugh conjecture setting)
